card.name: Article after study-result verbs
card.fires_on: The article "a" or "an" (sometimes the verb itself) right after a result verb such as demonstrated, reported, produced or showed. It appears in study findings and drug interaction text, just before a word like increased, significant or a percent change.

modes.label: Trial findings
modes.description: "an" after a verb like demonstrated or reported in summaries of a study's results, before "increased risk".
modes.example: The WHI estrogen plus progestin substudy demonstrated<< an>> increased risk of invasive breast cancer [see

modes.label: Interaction effects
modes.description: "a" after produced or was in drug interaction text, before a measured change.

modes.label: Result verb itself
modes.description: The result verb itself, when it is followed by the finding.
modes.example: discontinuation of rifampin<< produced>> a mean 3.3-fold increase

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words that describe a finding, such as significant, notable, marked and report.
card.plain: It marks the spot right after a phrase like "the study showed" where the size or direction of a finding comes next.
